name: Merge selected segments into the lowest selected class
answer: NO - Merge must NOT use the active class. Keep the executable behaviour, target = min(selected class ids), or next_class_id when none of the selected segments has a class; the docstrings that say 'assign selected segments to active class' are the defect and should not be ported. THE REASON IS WHICH STATE A USER IS LOOKING AT. Merge acts on segments the user has just selected and can see highlighted. The active class is a mode set somewhere else, possibly minutes ago, and possibly not on screen at all. Reading it here makes the same visible action produce different results depending on invisible state, which is the property that makes a destructive operation feel random. min(selected) is derivable from exactly what the user selected. IT IS ALSO THE LESS DESTRUCTIVE OF THE TWO. Merging classes 2 and 3 with class 7 active would move both to 7 - a class that took no part in the selection - so the operation would introduce a classification the user never asked for while removing two they had. min(selected) can only collapse toward a class that was already in the selection, so no new class appears and at least one segment keeps the class it had. THE ACTIVE CLASS ALREADY HAS ITS JOB. It governs CREATION: a new polygon, box, circle or accepted AI mask takes it. Merge is a reclassification of existing annotations, and reclassification already has a deliberate, explicit action in RULE-013 (reassign class ids from the class table order). Wiring the active class into merge as well would give two different controls for the same intent, one of them implicit. PRIORITY: not P0, and the panel was right. Nothing is deleted and no mask changes - masks stay separate, which the card states and the code confirms; only the class id moves, and it is recoverable both by the undo stack (RULE-052) and by an explicit reassign. It stays P1 because getting it wrong silently mislabels every merged object, which survives into every export. WHAT THE PORT MUST DO BESIDES: the docstring divergence is itself worth recording rather than quietly fixing, because someone reading legacy to check the port will hit it. The TypeScript implementation should name the rule in a comment - target is the lowest SELECTED class, not the active one - so the next reader does not resolve the contradiction the other way.
corrections: Answered the open SME question: Merge does not read the active class, and the docstrings that say it does are wrong.
Recorded why, in terms of which state is visible to the user at the moment they press M, rather than as a preference between two plausible behaviours.
Confirmed the panel's not-P0 rating with a reason: no data is destroyed, masks are untouched, and the change is undoable and explicitly reversible via RULE-013.
